title: "Comping rhythm: Strum: downstrokes on the beat"
subtitle: "For guitar, built up a step at a time"
toc: true
toc-depth: 2
---

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Strum: downstrokes on the beat**. It is built up from a simpler pattern, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

One ringing downstroke on every beat. The first strum to learn, and the usual one for a slow song.

It belongs in *Acoustic strum*, *Straight-eighth rock*, *Boom-chick*, *Piano ballad*, *Folk carol* and *Emo / pop-punk*. Here it is in the acoustic strum style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: Long notes

Start with something simpler. One held chord per bar (or per chord). Leaves the most room for a soloist.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-pad.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"Long notes","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: Strum: downstrokes on the beat, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Four downstrokes a bar, from the wrist, the hand moving down on every beat. Let each strum ring into the next. This is the motion every other strum is built on: the hand keeps going down on the beat.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="68" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}},{"label":"Long notes (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"pad"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 96 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C|G|Am|F" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="strum" data-chart="C G|Am F|C G|F G" data-tempo="96" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: In 3/4

The same pattern in a waltz: three beats to the bar. Listen for what it keeps and what it drops when the bar is a beat shorter.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="waltz" data-chart="C|C|F|F|G7|G7|C|C" data-tempo="120" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-meter="3/4" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Strum: downstrokes on the beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"strumQuarters"}}]'></div>

## In other styles
